newsitem.title: SWEDEN: TENNIS-ENQVIST BEATS FROMBERG IN STOCKHOLM OPEN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-ENQVIST BEATS FROMBERG IN STOCKHOLM OPEN.

text.p: Swedish number one Thomas Enqvist became one of only two of the world's top 20 tennis players left in the Stockholm Open on Wednesday when he beat Australian Richard Fromberg in the first round.
In a match lasting only 51 minutes, the 22-year-old Enqvist, who is ranked eighth in the world, defeated Fromberg 6-3 6-1.

The win boosted Enqvist's hopes of qualifying for the reserve berth in the ATP world championship in Hanover on November 19, where the year's eight top-scoring players compete in the world's most lucrative tournament.
Enqvist, who beat Russia's Yevgeny Kafelnikov to take the Paris Open title last Sunday, will play American Chris Woodruff in the second round in Stockholm on Thursday.
The tournament was suffering a dearth of top names, with only two of the top 20 left from seven in the starting line-up.
South Africa's Wayne Ferreira, ranked 10th, was bundled out in the first round on Monday by Britain's Greg Rusedski.
American Todd Martin, ranked 12th, remains in the field and will play compatriot Richey Reneberg in the quarter-finals on Friday.
Spaniard Albert Costa, ranked 13th, was beaten by Germany's Alex Radulescu who now faces Austria's Gilbert Schaller for a place in the quarter-finals.
Stefan Edberg, 14th in the ATP rankings and playing his last singles tournament, was defeated by fellow Swede Nicklas Kulti in straight sets on Tuesday.
Sweden's other top-ranked player, Magnus Gustafsson, 17th in the world, pulled out of the tournament late on Wednesday because of a stomach muscle injury.
He was replaced by South African 23-year-old qualifier Marcus Ondruska who then lost in the first round to Belgium's Filip Dewulf 6-1 6-4.
The world's 18th-ranked player, Dutchman Jan Siemerink, was beaten in the second round on Wednesday, by Denmark's Vincent Spadea 6-4 6-7 6-3.
